name: Salman Butt
feedback: D1 is a model findings catalogue. You caught all ten canonical issues and then some, each with the correct OWASP class, a sound CWE, and a quoted line from the actual pack: SQLi A03/CWE-89 at login.php:64-67 reconciled to the 02:15:31 302, unsalted MD5 A02/CWE-916, the hardcoded sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 secret A05/CWE-798, alg:none A07/CWE-347 tied to Token2, no exp/nbf A07/CWE-613, stored XSS A03/CWE-79 with the 185.220.101.9:8443 cookie beacon, XXE A05/CWE-611, path traversal A01/CWE-22 with the root:x:0:0 body, open redirect A01/CWE-601, and the cookie flags. Your decoy work is exactly right: you named the hash_equals HS256 branch, proved it constant-time at the mechanism level, and correctly kept alg:none and the hardcoded secret as the real bugs rather than mislabeling alg:none as the safe construct, which is the trap that catches weaker reports. D2 is strong with every hop in order and reconciled to its capture timestamp, verbatim PoCs throughout, and a business-impact section that does what we wanted, 312 customers and roughly NGN 75 million with the representative-sample assumption stated openly and the BoltCash six-week window named. The one thing to fix in D2 is the SQLi CVSS vector: you scored AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:L at 9.4, but an authentication bypass does not degrade availability, so A:N is correct and the score lands nearer 9.1. Treating administrative functionality becoming available as an availability impact is the common misread to avoid. D3 is a full-marks report: jargon-free exec summary that ends on the customers-and-naira headline, a real threat model that names the internal service sharing the JWT scheme, the decoy disproved correctly, the earliest-break fix argued at the login SQLi, and remediation ordered by effort-to-risk rather than CVSS severity, with XXE at hours ranked ahead of stored XSS and two concrete detection stopgaps carrying exact fields and false-positive rates. D4 answers all four prompts in your own voice, anchors to your own findings, and cites ISC2 Canon I and Canon II by number and load-bearing. The only gap across the whole submission is in D4: you named the NDPA 2023 breach duty and described it accurately, notify the NDPC within the statutory window and notify data subjects on high risk, but you did not cite the sections by number, which are Section 40 for the 72-hour NDPC notification and Section 41 for data-subject notification on high risk. Add those two section numbers and this deliverable is airtight. The single most important fix is small: cite NDPA Sections 40 and 72 hours and Section 41 by number in D4, and correct the SQLi availability metric to A:N.
